Description.DefaultValue: Mark Vedic recitation text in Word: holdings, svaras, reading aids and pauses, in the same notation and the same styles as the śikṣāmitra editor.

bt:String.DefaultValue: Mark the selected letters, or the letter before the caret.
Everything is on the śikṣāmitra tab. Type a letter and press Short or Long, or a svara — or right-click a selection.
Long vowels, vocalic ṛ and ḷ, the anusvāra and the visarga.
The consonants, by where they are spoken: gutturals to sibilants.
Vedic signs, accents and punctuation: ḻ, ꣳ, the daṇḍas and the avagraha.
Write the mantra lines in IAST, Devanāgarī, Telugu or Tamil — the selected ones, or the whole document when nothing is selected. Every mark is kept, and IAST again gives back exactly what was there.
Which śākhā’s rules mark the text here — the part the caret is in, the lines selected (they become a part), or the lines outside every part. One file may hold parts of different śākhās.
A short holding: a thin box around the letters. With nothing selected, the letter before the caret. Press again to take it off. (Ctrl+H)
A long holding: a thick box around the letters. With nothing selected, the letter before the caret. Press again to take it off. (Ctrl+Shift+H)
Take the holding off the letters, and leave every other marking. With nothing selected, the letter before the caret. (Ctrl+K)
The low tone: a bar under the letter. With nothing selected, the letter before the caret. Press again to take it off.
The raised tone: a stroke over the letter. With nothing selected, the letter before the caret. Press again to take it off.
The long raised tone: two strokes over the letter. With nothing selected, the letter before the caret. Press again to take it off.
These letters are recited in place of an anusvāra (ṁ), and are drawn in the change colour. With nothing selected, the letter before the caret.
These letters are recited in place of a visarga (ḥ), and are drawn in the change colour. With nothing selected, the letter before the caret.
The nasal m̐: the candrabindu laid on the letter. With nothing selected, the letter before the caret. Press again to take it off.
The svarabhakti dot, at the caret: between an r and the sibilant or h after it (var·ṣa).
A short pause at the caret: one bar.
A long pause at the caret: two bars.
Take every marking off the selected letters: holdings, svaras, changes, aids and pauses.
Every IAST letter and Vedic sign on one keyboard. Press a letter for its long or dotted form (a → ā, t → ṭ), or click a key. (Ctrl+Shift+I)
Type ṁ at the caret — anusvāra.
Type ḥ at the caret — visarga.
Type ḻ at the caret — Dravidian ḻ.
Type ṃ at the caret — anusvāra, alternate form.
Type ॥ at the caret — double daṇḍa.
Type ꣳ at the caret — Vedic tiryak.
Type a̱ at the caret — anudātta (U+0331).
Type a̍ at the caret — svarita (U+030D).
Type a̎ at the caret — dīrgha svarita (U+030E).
Type m̐ at the caret — candrabindu (U+0310).
Type ꣻ at the caret — Vedic anusvāra above (U+A8FB).
Type a̅ at the caret — Ṛgvedic overline (U+0305).
Type ˎ at the caret — virāma tick (U+02CE).
Type ऽ at the caret — avagraha.
Write the selected mantra lines in IAST, or the whole document when nothing is selected.
Write the selected mantra lines in Devanāgarī, or the whole document when nothing is selected.
Write the selected mantra lines in Telugu, or the whole document when nothing is selected.
Write the selected mantra lines in Tamil, or the whole document when nothing is selected.

Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda, the Taittirīya śākhā — Śrī Rudram, Puruṣa Sūktam, Durgā Sūktam, Mantra Puṣpam. Accents are taken from the source as written, and an anusvāra before a sibilant or h is shown as gṁ / gm.
Texts recited in a Ṛgvedic śākhā, in its own accentuation. Accents are taken from the source as written, and the anusvāra keeps its own form rather than becoming a g-form.
Vājasaneyi texts — Rudrāṣṭādhyāyī and the Mādhyandina recension. As Taittirīya, including the g-forms, over the Śukla recension’s own accentuation.

Stotras, aṣṭakas, nāmāvalīs, āgamic and purāṇic verse — Lalitā and Viṣṇu Sahasranāma. No accents are read from the source; the metre supplies them, the anusvāra is left as it is, and no semivowel aids are added.
Give the selected lines rules of their own — a sūkta of another śākhā among the others. Word draws a frame around the part, titled with its register.
Undo the part the caret is in: its lines stay, and the rules of the lines outside every part apply to them again.
Run the marking rules over the selection, or over the whole document when nothing is selected. What you placed by hand stays. (Ctrl+Shift+R)
Run the marking rules and DROP what you placed by hand, over the selection or the whole document.
Bring the śikṣāmitra styles into this document — the mantra line, the translation, the holdings, the svaras and the rest — so it looks like a Veda Union document.
Add the styles and a short marked passage at the end of the document, to see every mark as Word draws it.
The register and which rules run, the styles in this document, and the keyboard shortcuts — in the side panel.
The notation, mark by mark, in the browser.
